rows.title: Add local preview environments for main and per-ticket branches
rows.next: build since 2026-11-21 5:55 am UTC: spec approved; building local preview environments

sections.name: Goal
sections.text: One command runs the app from `main`, and one command per ticket runs the app from that ticket's worktree on its own port, side by side. Each preview has its own SQLite file, so a branch's migrations or test data never reach the main preview.

sections.name: Out of scope
sections.text:
- Deploying anywhere (#14), browser test runs and event capture (#19), shared or hosted preview URLs, CI preview builds.
- Creating worktrees. The script previews worktrees that exist; it does not make one for a ticket that has none.
- Windows. The script uses process groups and `lsof` hints; the user is on macOS.

sections.name: Calls I made
sections.text:
Surprising first.

- **The main preview uses the root checkout's real data file**, `data/album-ranker.db`, shared with `npm run dev` there, not a separate preview file. Main is merged code, so it's safe to run against real data, and the preview then shows what the user actually has. Ticket previews never touch that file except to read it for `--copy-main-data`.
- **The main preview is a production build** (`next build` + `next start`) and ticket previews run `next dev`. Main should look like what ships; a ticket preview should pick up edits while an agent works.
- **The script doesn't pull `main`.** It warns when the root checkout is behind `origin/main` and prints the pull command. Pulling would write to the root checkout from a preview command.
- **Previews run in the background** with a pid file and log, and stop through `npm run preview -- stop`, rather than in the foreground with Ctrl-C. Several previews at once in one terminal needs that.
- **Port 4000 for main, 4000 + N for tickets.** Simple to work out in your head; 3000 stays for plain `npm run dev`.
- **A ticket preview keeps its data between runs** unless `--empty` or `--copy-main-data` is passed.
- **One Node TypeScript script** rather than a shell script, to match `scripts/migrate.ts` and to unit test the rules.
- **The ticket match is on `album-<N>-` in the branch name**, the repo's branch pattern, not on the worktree folder name, since T3's folders are random ids.

rows.title: Import the existing spreadsheet
rows.next: build since 2026-11-21 5:46 am UTC: spec approved; building the spreadsheet import

sections.name: Goal
sections.text:
Load the user's `Best Albums.xlsx` into the app once, so years of rankings are not retyped. A command-line script reads the Albums sheet, matches each row to a MusicBrainz album, and writes year entries and decade list entries. Rows it can't match with confidence go to a review page in the app, where the user picks the album, keeps the row as a manual album, or skips it.

The spreadsheet stays out of the repo. Tests use a small fixture of made-up rows.

sections.name: Non-goals
sections.text:
- The artist rollup sheets, weighted scores and the candidate flag.
- Exporting back to a spreadsheet.
- Undoing a review resolution, or a "re-import from scratch" option.
- Importing any sheet but Albums, or a file other than `.xlsx`.

sections.name: Calls I made
sections.text:
- **The rank-plus-honorable-mention row is imported as an honorable mention and named in the summary, without a review item.** The ticket says it "goes to the review page"; the later MVP spec says no review item, because the placement is settled. I followed the MVP spec. If you'd rather review it, it becomes a fifth review reason.
- **A migration adds three columns:** a source decade rank on year entries (so decade lists come out in sheet order even when review items are resolved out of order), and a reason plus detail on review items (so the page can say why a row is there).
- **The catalog result gains the artist's MusicBrainz ids**, so imported albums by the same artist share one artist. This touches `lib/catalog/` from #5.
- **Clear match means equal normalized title and artist.** The normalizing rules above are mine. When there are several, a release year within one year of the sheet's year breaks the tie.
- **An exact match is accepted even if MusicBrainz's release year is far from the sheet's year.** The sheet's year always wins as the year page.
- **Catalog errors leave the row for the next run** instead of sending it to review, so a busy MusicBrainz doesn't fill the review page.
- **Exact duplicates ignore case**; the first row wins when merged rows differ.
- **A rank repeated within a year** sends the second row to review.
- **Columns are found by header name**, and the input `Rank` is the one right of `Album`. Checked against the header row of the user's file; no rows from it are in the spec or tests.
- **The review page lives at `/import`**, linked from the home page only while items are open. No undo.
- **A new dependency** to read `.xlsx`, read-only. Proposed: `read-excel-file`.
- **No dry-run mode.** A run takes about 15 minutes; a dry run would double that, and re-running is safe.

rows.title: Add frontend event tracking for replaying browser tests
rows.risk: Medium (new test tooling and dev dependency).
rows.next: build-queued since 2026-11-21 5:51 am UTC: spec approved, waiting for a build slot (builds running: ALBUM-7, ALBUM-10)

sections.name: Goal
sections.text:
While a browser test drives the app, record what the test does in the page (clicks, typing, form submits and route changes) as an ordered JSON event log, one file per test. The replay renderer, built elsewhere, reads that file and redraws the run.

The repo has no browser tests today, so this ticket also adds the browser test setup and one test of the search page, which is the run the Acceptance asks for.

sections.name: Non-goals
sections.text:
- The replay renderer.
- Recording real users or manual sessions, product analytics, sending events to any server.
- DOM snapshots, scroll, hover, mouse movement, key events other than through `input` and `submit`, screenshots or video.
- Changes to the database (`lib/db`).
- CI for browser tests. The repo has no CI yet.
- Browsers other than Chromium.

sections.name: Calls I made
sections.text:
Surprising first.

- **The event format is my proposal, not agreed with the renderer.** The ticket says to agree it with the renderer's thread before building. That thread isn't reachable from here and its format isn't in the repo, so the spec proposes version 1 above. If the renderer reads something else, change the format section before approving and the build follows it.
- **The recorder is injected by the browser test, not built into the app.** No app page or component changes, and nothing in the app bundle can record. Manual sessions can't be recorded.
- **This ticket adds Playwright and the first browser test**, since there were none to record. That brings a dev dependency and a one-time Chromium download.
- **One small app change: `MUSICBRAINZ_URL`**, so the browser test talks to a local stub instead of the live MusicBrainz. Without it the test would hit the live service, and MusicBrainz's 1 request per second limit and busy 503s would make it flaky.
- **Typing is one event per input event, holding the field's whole value**, not keystrokes. Paste and autofill show up the same way, and the renderer just sets the value.
- **Password values are masked** even though no password field exists yet.
- **The log is written per test**, to Playwright's output folder and attached to the report, not to a fixed folder in the repo.
- **Timestamps come from the browser clock**, relative to the test start, so a full page load doesn't reset them.
- **Element description is a CSS selector plus tag, id, name, role, label and text**, so the renderer can find the element by selector and fall back to the readable fields.
- **Chromium only.**

rows.title: Build the per-year ranking screen with drag and drop and covers
rows.risk: High (writes year placements to the data layer, new @dnd-kit dependency, calls that change ranking behaviour).
rows.next: build-queued since 2026-11-21 6:01 am UTC: spec approved, waiting for a build slot (builds running: ALBUM-10, ALBUM-20; ALBUM-19, ALBUM-8 queued first)

sections.name: Goal
sections.text: One page per year where the user builds that year's ranking by dragging album covers: a top 10, honorable mentions, and a list of albums heard that year but not placed. It replaces the spreadsheet's "Ranked" sheet. Every change saves straight away, and each rated album shows its current Elo rating.

sections.name: Out of scope
sections.text:
- Computing ratings (done in #7).
- Artist and decade views (#8, #9).
- Importing the spreadsheet (#10).
- Linking a manual album to a catalog album, and editing or deleting albums.
- End-to-end browser tests (the repo has no browser test setup).
- Undo for year edits.

sections.name: Calls I made
sections.text:
Surprising first.

- **Ranks always save without gaps.** Moving rank 4 to rank 1 renumbers the list 1 to N. A year with stored gaps keeps them on screen until its first edit, which closes them. The ticket's "shifts the others down by one" implies an ordered list; it doesn't mention gaps.
- **A full ranked list pushes rank 10 to honorable mentions** when an eleventh album is dropped in, and says so. The alternative was refusing the drop. Adding from search into a full ranked list is disabled instead, since there is no drop position to honour.
- **Move up/down and "Move to" buttons on every card,** on top of drag and drop with keyboard and touch. They give a way that doesn't depend on drag gestures and let jsdom tests cover every move.
- **`@dnd-kit` is a new dependency** for drag and drop. Native HTML drag and drop has no touch or keyboard support.
- **Save on every change, whole year at once,** through the existing `setYearPlacements`, with an optimistic update that reverts on failure. No save button.
- **Honorable mentions and listed albums are shown sorted by artist, then title,** because they store no order. Dragging within those areas doesn't reorder them.
- **Adding from search puts a ranked album at the end of the list;** the user then drags it into place.
- **The server re-checks catalog results** it receives from the browser, and only accepts Cover Art Archive cover URLs.
- **Catalog albums are stored with the artist by name only,** since search results carry no artist catalog id. Two catalog albums by the same artist share one artist row through the existing name match for artists with no catalog id.
- **A `/years` index page** lists years with entries and has a "Go to year" field. The ticket only says "pick any year".
- **Previous and next year links** on each year page.
- **A year outside 1900 to 2100 is a 404,** matching the data model's year range.
- **The manual album form asks for an optional release year;** the year page's year is where it's placed. …

rows.title: Add artist views by decade and overall
rows.risk: Medium (two new read-only pages, 5 Builds bullets).
rows.next: build-queued since 2026-11-21 6:01 am UTC: spec approved, waiting for a build slot (builds running: ALBUM-10, ALBUM-20; ALBUM-19 queued first)

sections.name: Goal
sections.text: Rank artists by the engine's artist score, overall and one decade at a time, and let the user open an artist to see their albums. This replaces the spreadsheet's Artist Stats and Artist Summary sheets. Scores are computed from the replayed ratings on every request, so answering a matchup or changing a year's ranking shows up on the next page load.

sections.name: Out of scope
sections.text:
- The decade top 25 album lists (#9).
- Changing how artists are scored.
- Matching the spreadsheet's artist summary or its paired decade groups (60s and 70s, and so on). The app shows one decade at a time.
- Sorting the table by other columns, search or paging. About 390 artists fit on one page.
- Per-decade scores on the artist page.
- Splitting collaborations into separate artists.

sections.name: Calls I made
sections.text:
Surprising first.

- **Tied scores get separate ranks** (1, 2, 3), ordered by artist name, then id. The ticket doesn't say how ties rank; real ties are rare once ratings are unrounded.
- **The artist page lists listed albums too** (with "No rating"), so the user sees everything they placed. They count for nothing in the score. Albums with no year entry are left out.
- **The decade picker is a row of links with a `?decade=` query**, not a dropdown or a route per decade. It needs no client code and the back button works.
- **An invalid decade or artist id shows the not-found page** rather than falling back to the overall list.
- **The picker is fixed at 1950s to 2020s**, as the ticket says. An album placed in an earlier or later decade counts in the overall list but has no decade tab.
- **Scores show as whole numbers**; the engine keeps them unrounded, and ordering uses the unrounded value, so two artists shown at 1600 can be ranked 1 and 2.
- **The artist page shows only the overall score**, not per-decade scores.
- **Albums on the artist page are ordered by year**, then album id.
- **Column and label text:** "Rank", "Artist", "Score", "Rated albums", "Overall", "Ranked #3", "Honorable mention", "Listed", "No rating", "All artists".
- **The loader lives in `lib/artists.ts` without `server-only`**, matching `lib/ratings.ts`, so tests can call it. Pages still reach the database only through `getDb()`.
- **No cache.** Ratings are replayed on every request, as the matchup screen does.

sections.name: Summary
sections.text:
Adds the MVP requirements spec for the album ranker: one-person web app, SQLite, catalog search with covers, per-year ranking screen, head-to-head Elo ratings (single algorithm, seeded from the yearly ranks), artist and decade views, and a one-off spreadsheet import. The spec also records what the real `Best Albums.xlsx` formulas say, which differs from the ticket's description (752 rows, 81 listed-only rows, the year weight formula, two artist rollup rules).

Ticket: ALBUM-2 (https://github.com/dbeallor/album-ranker/issues/2)
Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-album-ranker-mvp.md`

Closes #2
